text:
lia: heads up — alert fired for hosted-usw2: GPU pool p95 queueing climbed above 300ms and admission throttle hit 85% over the last 10m. dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/hosts/gpu-pools

matt: saw that. looks correlated with several large batch jobs from a single tenant. which pool is the hotspot?

lia: pool-id: gpupool-usw2-004 (in the hosted shared tier). heatmap shows sustained slot occupancy + long tail on create_container latency.

sre-oncall-bot: ALERT: hosted-usw2 gpupool-usw2-004 admission throttle >= 80% for 12m. Incident runbook: /docs/runbooks/admission-throttle.md :rotating_light:

devon: can we temporarily relax admission_control from 0.85 -> 0.95 to let short requests through while we triage? downside is potential p99 latency increase.

jordan: before changing thresholds, can we evict or deprioritize that single tenant's queued jobs? I can run a query to find their job IDs.

matt: +1 to finding tenant jobs. also try routing overflow to euw1 if network egress is OK. we have capacity there.

lia: quick PromQL I used to spot the build-up:
```
sum by(pool) (gpu_queue_length{region="usw2"})
```
and this one for admission throttle:
```
sum by(pool) (admission_throttle_ratio{pool="gpupool-usw2-004"})
```

ops-automations: ran command to list in-flight jobs for tenant "acme-corp":
```
./infractl jobs list --pool gpupool-usw2-004 --owner acme-corp --state queued
```
returned 27 jobs (mix of long-continuation and short gen).

devon: propose immediate mitigations:
- pause or set owner-specific concurrency cap for acme-corp (limit 3)
- lower default max_batch_size from 64 -> 32 for gpupool-usw2-004 to reduce tail latency
- enable prefix KV cache for common model routes

lia: executed the owner concurrency cap (set to 3) and lowered max_batch_size to 32 via runtime config. monitoring now.

sre-oncall-bot: NOTE: runtime config change applied to gpupool-usw2-004 by lia at 2050001125.

jordan: after cap + batch change queue length dropped ~40% in last 3m. p95 down to ~220ms. still higher than target but trending down.

matt: good. I'll open a follow-up to throttle pipeline owners with large background jobs; maybe enforce job type labels so we can route them to dedicated or scheduled windows.

lia: long-term action items (added to infra board):
- add per-tenant queueing metrics to pool dashboard
- auto-schedule large batch jobs to low-traffic windows or dedicated pools
- inventory pools with <15% burst headroom across regions and plan refill/scale tests

ops-automations: created ticket INFRA-1428: "per-tenant queue metrics + automated overflow routing" and linked to this thread.

devon: also flagged cost note — routing overflow to euw1 increases egress and cross-region costs; add cost estimate to the ticket.

matt: thanks all. leaving monitoring open for 30m. if p95 < 150ms and admission_throttle < 25% we can close the alert. :thumbsup:

lia: will update if anything regresses. great triage team!
